# HELP scylla_manager_scheduler_last_success Start time of the last successful run as a Unix timestamp. The start time is reported, and not the end time, because it describes the state of the data the run worked on - a repair makes the data as fresh as of the moment it started, and a backup stores the snapshot taken at that moment.
# TYPE scylla_manager_scheduler_last_success gauge
scylla_manager_scheduler_last_success{cluster="b703df56-c428-46a7-bfba-cfa6ee91b976",task="965f4f5c-c7d1-4ae6-b770-a2225df4ef49",type="backup"} 1.645517563e+09

# HELP scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state State of the task, as "sctool tasks" reports it: 0 - never run, 1 - currently running, 2 - last run is done, 3 - last run ended in error, 4 - last run was stopped. A run aborted by a Scylla Manager restart, or cut short by the end of its maintenance window, reads as stopped.
